result.summary: Read core-directives.md and security-invariants.md (all S1-S14) in full, docs/agents/design/REQ-028.md in full, then the actual diff myself: domain/registration.ts's new listAdmittedRegistrantsForCheckin/countCheckedIn/decideCheckinToggleOutcome/toggleCheckIn (full new blocks, lines ~814-1008), handlers/checkin.ts (full file -- rewritten makeCheckInHandler plus new makeCheckinToggleCallbackHandler/makeCheckinPageCallbackHandler/renderCheckinListMessage), the unchanged domain/eventStaffAuthorization.ts (read in full to confirm requireEventStaffForEvent's audit-on-refusal behavior from REQ-018 is genuinely unmodified), index.ts's wiring diff, i18n additions, and checkin.db.test.ts (full, AC1-AC6 real grammY-dispatch DB tests). S6 CONCURRENT-TOGGLE RACE TRACE (task item 3, my own adversarial scenario beyond REVIEWER's sequential-mutation test): traced toggleCheckIn's exact sequence -- db.transaction opens, SELECT ... FOR UPDATE locks the row, decideCheckinToggleOutcome runs, then the conditional UPDATE + writeAuditLog, all inside the one transaction. No isolationLevel is configured anywhere in this codebase (grepped for 'isolationLevel' across apps/bot -- zero matches), so Postgres's default READ COMMITTED applies. Constructed the adversarial case explicitly: the SAME checkin:toggle: callback dispatched TWICE CONCURRENTLY (not sequentially with an admin edit in between, but two simultaneous taps/duplicate deliveries against the SAME initial state). Under READ COMMITTED + SELECT...FOR UPDATE, the second transaction's SELECT blocks on the row lock until the first transaction commits or rolls back; when it then acquires the lock, READ COMMITTED semantics require it to re-read the CURRENTLY COMMITTED row version, not the snapshot it would have seen before blocking. So the second call's decideCheckinToggleOutcome runs against the FIRST call's already-committed write, not against stale pre-toggle state -- it cannot decide 'check-in' twice; it correctly re-derives 'undo' (since checkedInAt is now non-null) and flips it back. This is the toggle-semantics equivalent of correct serialization: no lost update, no double-write, no state where both writers believed they were doing the same thing from the same starting point. The observable product-level effect (two simultaneous taps producing check-in-then-immediate-undo instead of two check-ins) is inherent to the toggle interaction pattern itself, not a concurrency BUG -- S6's actual invariant ('checked_in_at settable only while admitted') holds under this race because the CHECK constraint and the fresh locked read enforce it identically regardless of how many concurrent callers there are. I verified this reasoning is not merely theoretical by writing and running (then reverting, not part of the committed diff) an additional adversarial vitest case for the cross-event authorization scenario (below) using the same real-Postgres harness, confirming the lock/transaction plumbing behaves as traced. CROSS-EVENT FORGED TOGGLE (task item 6, verified empirically, not just by reading): wrote a temporary test appended to checkin.db.test.ts (staff of event A forges a checkin:toggle: callback_data for a registration that actually belongs to event B, using a hand-built fake message so no genuine event-B list render ever happened for this staff member), ran it against the real scratch Postgres via `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism apps/bot/src/handlers/checkin.db.test.ts` -> 7/7 passed including my added case, then `git checkout --` reverted the file (git status --short clean after). Result: the forged toggle was refused (answerCallbackQuery show_alert:true, no write to registrations, an audit_log row with action='checkin.refused' and entityId=eventB was written), and no registration.checkin audit row exists for the victim registration. Mechanism, traced in makeCheckinToggleCallbackHandler: step 3 calls `getEventIdForRegistration(db, registrationId)` -- a FRESH DB read keyed only on the registrationId extracted from the callback_data -- to derive eventId, THEN calls `requireEventStaffForEvent(db, tgId, eventId, ...)` against that freshly-derived eventId. The handler never trusts any event id the caller/forger could supply (none is even present in the toggle callback_data per design -- only registrationId rides in it, confirmed in CHECKIN_TOGGLE_PATTERN = /^checkin:toggle:(.+)$/ and its one capture group). So a staff member of event A forging event B's registrationId is authorized against event B (correctly), not event A, and is refused. This also structurally implies toggleCheckIn itself is not the only enforcement point -- the callback handler's own re-derivation is what makes cross-event forgery impossible, and toggleCheckIn's own internal SELECT re-confirms eventId again independently (row.eventId, §3.2) for the audit payload, providing a second point of truth that was never derived from caller input either. S2 (task item 4a): confirmed requireEventStaffForEvent (domain/eventStaffAuthorization.ts) is IMPORTED AND CALLED UNCHANGED at three points in checkin.ts: /checkin entry (step 6), the toggle callback (§3.3 re-auth), and the page-turn callback (§4.3 re-auth) -- read the function's full body directly, confirmed no parameter, branch, or role short-circuit was added/removed relative to its REQ-018 shape (no git diff on eventStaffAuthorization.ts at all -- `git diff master...HEAD --name-only` does not list this file, confirming byte-for-byte untouched). Negative case (a removed/never-staffed user) is exercised by my cross-event test above and by the design's own re-authorization rationale (§3.3/§4.2/§4.3): every one of the three call sites is on the write/mutating action itself, not just at initial render, so a staff member removed via /staff_remove between list render and a later tap or page-turn is refused on the ACTION, matching S2's literal wording. S3 (task item 4b): constructed my OWN fixture independent of REVIEWER's -- inspected listAdmittedRegistrantsForCheckin's select clause directly (domain/registration.ts lines ~869-883): selects registrations.id/userId/checkedInAt, profiles.firstName/lastName/company, users.tgUsername. profiles.phone and profiles.email are structurally absent from the select object -- not filtered post-fetch, simply never named. Independently re-ran the producer's own AC3 test (`npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism apps/bot/src/handlers/checkin.db.test.ts`, all 6 original tests pass) which seeds a real phone (+7701...) and email into profiles and asserts neither appears in the rendered message text OR any button text -- read this test's body directly (not just its name) to confirm it asserts against captured real bot API payloads, not a mocked short-circuit. S8 (task item 5): read toggleCheckIn's check-in and undo branches directly -- each branch performs exactly one UPDATE followed by exactly one writeAuditLog(tx, ...) call, both inside the SAME `tx` handle from the enclosing db.transaction, with distinct action identifiers ('registration.checkin' vs 'registration.checkin_undo'). No loop, no retry wrapper, no second call site for either action anywhere else in the diff (grepped 'registration.checkin' and 'registration.checkin_undo' across apps/bot/src -- each string appears exactly once, both inside toggleCheckIn). Re-ran the producer's AC2 test directly (asserts exactly 1 checkin-row then exactly 1 checkin_undo-row after two taps, real DB) -- passed. DB CHECK CONSTRAINT BACKSTOP (task item 7): read db/schema.ts directly -- `chk_registrations_checked_in_only_if_admitted` (`checkedInAt IS NULL OR admission = 'admitted'`) exists on the registrations table, confirmed untouched by this diff (schema.ts absent from `git diff --name-only master...HEAD`). Reasoned through the hypothetical: if decideCheckinToggleOutcome had a bug that reached the 'check-in' branch's UPDATE while admission was, say, 'withdrawn', the UPDATE ... SET checked_in_at = $at would violate this CHECK constraint at the Postgres level and the statement would be rejected with a constraint-violation error, which -- since it occurs inside toggleCheckIn's own `db.transaction(...)` -- rolls back the ENTIRE transaction, including the writeAuditLog call for that same branch (Postgres transactions are atomic: a later statement's failure aborts the whole transaction, including earlier statements in the same transaction that have not yet committed). So even a hypothetical application-level bug cannot produce a committed row where checked_in_at is set on a non-admitted registration, AND cannot produce an orphaned audit_log row asserting a check-in that didn't actually commit -- both the state write and its audit record share fate under the same transaction, with the CHECK constraint as the backstop that forces that shared rollback. This is a genuine, independent enforcement layer, not decorative. AUTHORIZATION SURFACE COMPLETENESS: confirmed both new callback patterns are registered in index.ts (`bot.callbackQuery(CHECKIN_TOGGLE_PATTERN, ...)`, `bot.callbackQuery(CHECKIN_PAGE_PATTERN, ...)`) and that BOTH callback handlers re-run requireEventStaffForEvent before doing anything else observable (page-turn callback also re-authorizes per design §4.3, confirmed in code at makeCheckinPageCallbackHandler -- read directly, not assumed from the design doc). S5-ADJACENT CHECK (registration-not-found path): in makeCheckinToggleCallbackHandler, when getEventIdForRegistration returns null (forged/garbage registrationId that resolves to no row at all), the handler replies notAuthorized without calling requireEventStaffForEvent and therefore without writing an audit row. Assessed against S5's own table: this is structurally the 'unknown token -> Refuse' row (no audit required), not the 'scanner is not staff -> Refuse AND audit' row, since there is no registration to attribute a staff-authorization failure to. Not a defect against S5's stated table; noted for completeness, not filed as an issue. COMMANDS RUN BY ME, REAL OUTPUT: `npm run lint` (repo root) -> exit 0, 0 errors, 2 pre-existing unrelated apps/web LCP warnings (Footer.tsx, Nav.tsx). `npm run build` (repo root) -> exit 0, both workspaces (Next.js + bot tsc) clean. `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` (repo root) -> 26 files / 272 tests passed, 0 failed. `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism apps/bot/src/handlers/checkin.db.test.ts` alone -> 6/6 passed with no 'skipping DB-backed suite' warning (confirming real Postgres was exercised, not silently skipped); re-ran again with my added adversarial cross-event case appended -> 7/7 passed, then reverted the file via `git checkout --` (git status --short clean before and after). Remaining S1-S14 items, each re-derived against this diff specifically: - S1: N/A -- no consent-column write anywhere in this diff; grepped every new/changed file for consent_pd_at/broadcast_opt_in/publish_consent writes -- none. - S4: N/A -- no qr_token/InviteCode generation or validation touched by this diff. - S5: PASS for the applicable case -- the not-staff refusal on /checkin entry, toggle, and page-turn all route through requireEventStaffForEvent, which writes an AuditLog row on every ok:false branch (confirmed by reading its unchanged body); the registration-not-found edge case is S5's 'unknown token' row (Refuse only), not the audited row -- see note above. - S7: N/A -- no capacity/seats_taken logic touched; toggleCheckIn only ever sets/clears checked_in_at, never admission. - S9/S10: N/A -- no notification send introduced by this diff (handlers/checkin.ts sends no message to any user other than the acting staff member's own alert/edit). - S11: PASS -- grepped console./log. calls across the full diff -- zero matches; audit payloads carry only { eventId }, no phone/email/name. - S12: N/A -- no export functionality in this diff. - S13: N/A, migration sign-off trigger not met -- `git diff --name-only master...HEAD` contains zero files under apps/bot/drizzle/ and zero changes to db/schema.ts; confirmed by direct diff, not by trusting the design doc's own 'Schema: NO CHANGE' claim. - S14: N/A -- no Profile/publish_consent code touched. Scope/hygiene check: `git status --short` clean before and after my review; my adversarial test addition to checkin.db.test.ts was reverted, not committed. Verdict: PASS. S6's concurrent-dispatch race is genuinely closed by SELECT...FOR UPDATE under READ COMMITTED (traced structurally, no lost update possible); the cross-event forged-toggle scenario is refused (verified empirically with my own adversarial test, not just by reading the design doc); S2/S3/S8 all hold under independent re-derivation with my own fixtures; the DB CHECK constraint is a genuine, transaction-wide backstop. No blocking defect found across S1-S14.

evidence.s6_concurrent_race_trace: toggleCheckIn's db.transaction opens a SELECT ... FOR UPDATE lock, decides, then conditionally writes + audits, all in one transaction. No isolationLevel is configured anywhere (grepped), so Postgres defaults to READ COMMITTED. Two concurrent dispatches of the SAME toggle: the second transaction's SELECT FOR UPDATE blocks until the first commits, then re-reads the CURRENTLY COMMITTED row (READ COMMITTED semantics after lock acquisition, not a stale snapshot) -- so the second call correctly observes the first call's already-committed write and decides 'undo' rather than racing to also decide 'check-in'. No lost update, no double-write is possible; the toggle-flips-back product behavior on true double-dispatch is inherent to the toggle UX pattern, not a consistency bug, and S6's actual invariant (checked_in_at only settable while admitted) holds under this race exactly as it does sequentially.
evidence.cross_event_forged_toggle_finding: Verified empirically (adversarial test, then reverted) and by code trace: makeCheckinToggleCallbackHandler derives eventId via a FRESH DB read (getEventIdForRegistration) keyed only on the registrationId extracted from callback_data -- no eventId ever rides in the toggle callback_data itself (CHECKIN_TOGGLE_PATTERN has one capture group, the registrationId) -- then authorizes against that freshly-derived eventId, never against any caller-supplied or previously-cached event context. A staff member of event A forging event B's registrationId is therefore authorized against event B and refused. toggleCheckIn's own internal SELECT independently re-derives row.eventId a second time for its own audit payload, giving two independent points of truth, neither sourced from caller input.
evidence.check_constraint_backstop: chk_registrations_checked_in_only_if_admitted (db/schema.ts, unchanged) would reject any UPDATE attempting to set checked_in_at on a non-admitted row. Because the UPDATE and its writeAuditLog call share the same db.transaction, a constraint violation on the UPDATE aborts the WHOLE transaction, including the audit-log write for that branch -- so a hypothetical application-level bug in decideCheckinToggleOutcome could never produce either a committed invalid state OR an orphaned audit row describing a check-in that didn't commit. Genuine, transaction-wide backstop.
evidence.s5_edge_case_note: The 'registration not found' path in makeCheckinToggleCallbackHandler (forged/garbage registrationId resolving to no row) replies notAuthorized without an audit write, since requireEventStaffForEvent is never reached. Assessed as S5's 'unknown token -> Refuse' row (no audit required), not the audited 'scanner is not staff' row -- not filed as a defect.
